newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S-E-Banken, Nordbanken merger possible - analysts.
newsitem.headline: S-E-Banken, Nordbanken merger possible - analysts.

text.p: A merger between S-E-Banken and Nordbanken, two of Sweden's leading banks, is quite possible, analysts said on Tuesday after a Swedish newspaper report renewed rumours in the market.
"There's been a lot of talk about such a merger and it is fairly likely," one analyst told Reuters.
Both banks refused to comment on market speculation.
Rumours about such a merger have been in the market for some time alongside speculation about other large moves in Sweden's bank sector which is seen as ripe for restructuring.
This was further fuelled by banking group Handelsbanken placing a 22.9 billion crown bid for mortgage bank Stadshypotek last Thursday.
Analysts on the whole approved the merger between S-E-Banken and Nordbanken saying they complemented each other.
While Nordbanken focuses on private customers, small companies and municipalities, S-E-Banken focuses on large companies and investment banking.
"Nordbanken also has a very good distribution network as it cooperates with the postal service and has a large telephone bank," said Fredrik Myren, analyst at HSBC James Capel.

And although both banks have fewer branch offices than rivals Handelsbanken, Swedbank and Foreningsbanken, a merger is likely to lead to large synergies as both have branch offices in the same cities, analysts say.
A merger would also mean that the banks could share IT investments.
"IT costs are becoming more and more significant as more and more services are IT-based and after a merger the banks could share the costs," Myren said.
Analysts did not think a merger would cost the group market share in the long-term.
"Initially, the merged bank could lose market share as the merger will make it vulnerable, but it will become such a strong player that it should be able to recover it," Myren said.
Swedish financial daily Dagens Industri on Tuesday said the two banks had been in talks all weekend and that they could announce a merger before the end of the year.
But the Finance Ministry told Reuters that this was pure speculation.
With the state holding 59 percent of equity and votes in Nordbanken, the Finance Ministry would have to be informed about an imminent merger plan.
Analysts doubted the banks would move as quickly as in the next couple of weeks.
"I do not see the need for being in such a hurry," an analyst said.
Other analysts agreed, but said that banks were under pressure to become larger ahead of Europe's planned Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), which is due to start in 1999.

"Everyone is calculating on mergers with everyone, as all are under pressure from EMU," an analyst said. "When EMU is a fact, Swedish banks will face competitors that are ten times larger than they are. They need to grow."
The newspaper article said the if the deal goes through, S-E-Banken will act as a buyer, but analysts are not so sure.
"A third party, say an international player, could buy the state's stake in Nordbanken and then bid for S-E-Banken," an analyst suggested.
